Hi all — quick prep note from the SE side. Thanks for sharing the checklist, Marissa. A few clarifications so we can make best use of the time on Tue Dec 8 if that’s the confirmed slot: 

1) Prompt samples: please include 8–12 typical prompts spanning the short / medium / long cases. A CSV is great (one prompt per line). If you have templated prompts with variables, include an example expanded instance.
2) Token distribution: the token-distribution spreadsheet should include approximate percentiles (p50, p90, p99) and an average sequence length for requests. That lets us pick batching and KV-cache strategies.
3) Workload traces: if infra can’t provide the full trace, a 24-hour sample with timestamps and token counts is sufficient for our cost sims.
4) Access: we’ll need a read-only S3/GCS link or a temporary shared Drive folder for larger artifacts. If you prefer, we can accept an anonymized S3 URL and the team will pull samples during prep.

If Tue Dec 8 at 9:00am PT is confirmed, I’ll prepare a short live run that demonstrates: model choice tradeoffs, batching sensitivity, and a quick quantization/latency comparison using your prompts. I’ll also attach a tiny prompt-parsing script that helps us reproduce examples quickly.

Attachments referenced: sample_prompt_set_v1.csv (csv), workload_traces_2026-11.zip (zip, stub)

Thanks — happy to adapt based on what infra can share.

Monica Patel
Solutions Engineer, Redwood Inference
